newsitem.title: BELGIUM: DELHAIZE CEO WANTS LONGER SHOP HOURS.
newsitem.headline: DELHAIZE CEO WANTS LONGER SHOP HOURS.

text.p: Gui De Vaucleroy, chief executive officer of Belgian retailer Delhaize, said on Wednesday he would like to see Belgian shops opening earlier and staying open later.
"We should also look at opening on Sundays," he said. "But these are very delicate matters."

Speaking at a seminar for Belgian financial analysts, he said it was essential that supermarket chains did what they could to cut queues at check-outs by extending shopping hours, greater use of technology and optimisation of shopping space.
Vaucleroy said his firm's studies had shown that the optimum sales floor space was around 2,000 square metres -- the average floor size of Delhaize's own stores.
Much bigger and shopping took too long, much smaller and the consumer was deprived of range and choice, he said.

He added that home delivery from telephoned or telefaxed orders was another avenue to be explored, but that to date it had proved difficult to persuade customers to pay much towards the extra costs entailed.
